Proposition
[Differential Bianchi Identity] ↗ prop:properties-normal-coordinates 1. ch7:7.13

On a Riemannian or pseudo-Riemannian manifold, egin{equation} abla Rm(X,Y,Z,V,W)+ abla Rm(X,Y,V,W,Z) + abla Rm(X,Y,W,Z,V)=0. ag {7.14} \end{equation} Equivalently, in components, egin{equation} R_{ijkl;m}+R_{ijlm;k}+R_{ijmk;l}=0. ag {7.15} \end{equation}

Proof

\sketch Curvature symmetries reduce (7.14) to

egin{equation} abla Rm(Z,V,X,Y,W)+ abla Rm(V,W,X,Y,Z) + abla Rm(W,Z,X,Y,V)=0. ag {7.16} \end{equation}

Fix $p$ and use normal coordinate vector fields $X,Y,Z,V,W$ at $p$. Their brackets vanish identically and their covariant derivatives vanish at $p$. Thus

\[ ( abla _WRm)(Z,V,X,Y) =\langle abla _W abla _Z abla _VX- abla _W abla _V abla _ZX,Y angle \quad ext{at }p. \]

Adding its cyclic permutations in $W,Z,V$ gives

\[ \left\langle R(W,Z)( abla _VX)+R(Z,V)( abla _WX)+R(V,W)( abla _ZX),Y ight angle =0 \]

at $p$. Multilinearity and the arbitrariness of $p$ prove the identity.

□
